songs.name: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: Electric Althea solo and blazing Wheel>Other One>Wharf Rat
ai_show_review.blurb: The September 23‑1982 New Haven show bursts with high‑energy playing, highlighted by a tight Wheel → Other One → Wharf Rat sequence and an inspired Althea. Jerry’s guitar is electric throughout, Phil’s bass cuts through unusually clearly, and Brent’s B‑3 organ fuels the momentum. The excellent Charlie Miller soundboard capture makes this one of the standouts from the early‑80s era.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at Veterans Memorial Coliseum on September 23, 1982 is a quintessential early‑‘80s Dead experience: the band rides a wave of electric intensity that never lets up. The first set builds solidly with a punchy Alabama Getaway and a gritty Little Red Rooster, but it’s the second set that truly shines. After a concise Touch of Grey, the group launches into a seamless Wheel → Other One → Wharf Rat jam that feels both tight and exploratory, propelled by Brent’s throbbing B‑3 and an especially crisp Phil Lesh bass line—rarely this audible for the period. Jerry Garcia delivers a soaring solo on Althea that sits alongside his “on” tone throughout, while Bob Weir adds tasteful slide work on Rooster and solid rhythm guitar elsewhere. The drummers, Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann, lock in during the post‑drum break, driving the jam forward into Space before the set closes with an exuberant Johnny B. Goode. The Charlie Miller soundboard recording captures every nuance—clear mix, balanced dynamics, and no dropouts—making it the definitive source for this high‑octane performance.

best_recording.reason: Charlie Miller soundboard offers excellent clarity, balanced mix, prominent Brent organ and unusually audible Phil bass, with no dropouts.

key_highlights: Blazing Wheel → Other One → Wharf Rat sequence with tight transitions
Electric Althea solo that showcases Jerry’s soaring lead work
Little Red Rooster features gritty guitar tone and standout slide from Bob
High‑energy second set driven by powerful drum break and Space

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia is fully “on” with an electric tone, delivering a standout solo on Althea and strong leads throughout the jam sections.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass is unusually forward in the mix, adding power and clarity that anchors the Wheel/Other One/Wharf Rat sequence.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s slide work shines on Little Red Rooster and his rhythm guitar stays solid, supporting the band’s momentum.
band_performance.Brent: Mydland’s B‑3 organ is prominent, providing a thick texture that fuels the high energy of the second set.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart contributes tight, driving rhythms during the drum break and maintains groove throughout the jams.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann locks in with Hart, delivering a crisp, propulsive beat that lifts the extended improvisations.
